questions.question: He presents with L leg swelling, erythema, pain 2 years later

parts.text: What is the most likely organism?
What are 3 interventions to decrease the risk of recurrence of this complication.

questions.model_answer:
a) Likely cause: recurrent cellulitis at the site of saphenous vein harvest (post-CABG), related to chronic lymphedema/venous insufficiency and portal of entry via tinea pedis.
b) Most likely organism: non-group A beta-hemolytic Streptococcus (group C, G, or B).
c) Three interventions to reduce recurrence: (1) Treat/prevent interdigital tinea pedis. (2) Compression stockings and limb elevation/skin hygiene to reduce lymphedema (lymphatic pneumatic compression if needed). (3) Prophylactic antibiotics (e.g., monthly benzathine penicillin or oral penicillin V) for patients with frequent recurrences.

questions.question: [image-based question: Picture of man with nodular lymphangitis. Has aquarium.]

parts.text: Give a differential of four possible causes of this clinical picture.
Given that he has an aquarium, which is most likely?

cohort_answer.text: Differential: Mycobacterium marinum; Sporothrix schenckii; Nocardia brasiliensis; Leishmania braziliensis; Tularemia; Systemic mycoses. Most likely: Mycobacterium marinum. Diagnosis: Biopsy for AFB and culture + histopath. Treatment: surgical debridement/excision should suffice, if invasive, give rifampin + ethambutol +/- macrolide

questions.question: Child with single cervical LN enlargement.

parts.text: What is the most likely pathogen (to species)?
How do you make the diagnosis?

cohort_answer.text: Pathogen: Mycobacterium avium complex. Diagnosis: Biopsy for AFB culture/histopathology. Optimal management: Surgical resection; if abx needed: Clarithromycin, rifampin/ethambutol

questions.question: 24-year old with left neck fluctuant mass. It is warm, and erythematous and the patient is febrile. Name the pathogen and the MOST APPROPRIATE sample and method of diagnosis.

parts.text: Variant: He was bit in the neck by a rabbit
Variant: He just immigrated from the Phillipines and also describes weight loss.
Variant: He ate steak tartare 1 week prior
Variant: He has a sore throat with exudate

questions.model_answer: Base case (fluctuant, warm, erythematous neck mass, febrile - acute suppurative lymphadenitis): pathogen Staphylococcus aureus (or Streptococcus pyogenes); sample/method - needle aspiration of the fluctuant node for Gram stain and culture. a) Rabbit bite variant: Francisella tularensis (tularemia) - or Pasteurella multocida; sample/method - lymph node aspirate/biopsy for culture (notify lab given F. tularensis biosafety risk) and/or serology (acute and convalescent tularemia serology). b) Philippines immigrant with weight loss variant: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (scrofula/TB lymphadenitis); sample/method - fine-needle aspiration or excisional lymph node biopsy for AFB smear, mycobacterial culture, and NAAT (Xpert MTB/RIF). c) Steak tartare variant: Toxoplasma gondii (toxoplasmic lymphadenitis from undercooked meat); sample/method - serology (Toxoplasma IgM/IgG), as histology alone is nonspecific and organism isolation from lymph node is not typically performed. d) Sore throat with exudate variant: Group A Streptococcus (Streptococcus pyogenes) - or Epstein-Barr virus if mononucleosis suspected; sample/method - throat swab for rapid antigen/culture (or heterophile antibody/Monospot test if EBV suspected).

questions.question: Kid from Ottawa with swollen cervical lymph node. Biopsy shows caseating granuloma. Not improving on antibiotics.

parts.text: What is the treatment of choice?

cohort_answer.text: NTM (MAC, M. scrofulaceum) or TB (non-caseating granuloma ddx includes Bartonella, Toxoplasma, Syphilis, EBV, Tularemia, dimorphic fungi, Cryptococcus). Treatment of choice: Surgical resection

questions.question: There is a previously well 6-year-old who presents with unilateral tender inguinal lymphadenopathy, with a history of trauma to her thigh. The LN is sampled and grows a beading branching GPB.

parts.text: What is the most likely cause (Genus only)
Three antibiotics that will cover it.

cohort_answer.text: Cause: Actinomyces (israelii). Antibiotics: Penicillin G; Amoxicillin; Ceftriaxone (if non-beta lactam: doxy, clinda)
